text:
yun: heads-up — noticed increased preemptions in us-west1 between 02:00-05:00 last night, interactive latency spikes for sessions pinned to preemptible pool :alarm_clock:

mike: yep saw that, batch evictions causing noisy neighbor on interactivity. cost saved but UX hit :grimacing:

alexa: what's current policy for interactive fallback? Are we auto-failing to on-demand or queued?

yun: current is to retry 3x with backoff and route to on-demand only if request is flagged high-priority. Low-priority interactive gets queued into warm-pool for 30s.

jordan: can we change to immediate fallback for user-facing calls after 1 preemption? net satisfaction beats $ per token.

mike: problem is capacity — on-demand pool is tiny in eu-west due to budget caps; routing would overload it and cause more latency.

alexa: maybe use mixed-capacity: reserve small hot on-demand buffer per region for interactive, plus opportunistic spot pool for background.

sre-bot: alert triggered: preemptions in us-west1 x 125 in 1h window. See dashboards: https://dash.rew/evict

yun: proposal: implement time-windowed off-peak shift — during 00:00-06:00 shift more batch to spot-only lanes, shrink interactive concurrency, and spin extra on-demand if preemption rate > 10%.

mike: +1. also add per-queue eviction credit tracking so batch jobs with high makespan get preemption-safeguarded (checkpointing).

alexa: sample config sketch:
```
queue: interactive
priority: high
fallback: on-demand
fallback-after-preemptions: 1
warm-pool: 30s
```

and
```
queue: batch
priority: low
spot-only: true
checkpoint: 15m
max-retries: 5
```

mike: we'll need autoscaler rules too: if preemptions spike -> scale up warm on-demand to maintain p99 latency < 600ms. Use regional budget jitter to avoid cross-region thrashing.

jordan: FYI, network egress quotas in ap-south are tight — we should avoid shifting large batch output there during rebalances.

yun: action items:
- mike: prototype per-queue eviction-credit metric + dashboard (due 3d)
- alexa: update router to allow 2-tier fallback (immediate -> on-demand, delayed -> queued) (due 5d)
- jordan: sanity-check region budgets & advise cap increases if needed (due 4d)

mike: noted. I'll post PR with config and k8s taint example:
```
kubectl taint nodes spot=true:PreferNoSchedule
```

alexa: thanks. Also can we add a canary in eu-west before global rollout? small % of traffic for 24h.

yun: agreed. let's do canary + SLO guardrails. :white_check_mark:

mike: any objections to moving forward?

jordan: none from infra side. :+1:

alexa: no objections. will sync with product about UX tradeoffs.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: started canary rollout for interactive-fallback-policy -> 3 nodes eu-west at 2026-03-18T09:30Z

mike: will follow up with perf numbers during canary.
